intro: Searching for critical illness insurance near you usually means you want to know how a lump sum would work if you were diagnosed with a serious illness, and who locally can explain the options properly. Critical illness cover pays a lump sum if you are diagnosed with a specified serious illness, and the detail matters, so a conversation with an insurance broker can help you understand what you are comparing.
need_heading: What people searching for critical illness insurance near me usually need
need_lead: Most people who type this search want plain answers about cover before they commit to anything.
needs: You want to understand what counts as a specified serious illness under different policies, because definitions vary by insurer.
You are thinking about how a lump sum could help with costs if you became seriously ill, such as adapting your home or covering time away from work.
You have children and want to know whether children's cover is included, since it often is.
You are unsure how much cover is sensible for your circumstances and want help working through it.
You want to speak to someone local who can explain exclusions and how they are paid before you decide.
context_heading: Understanding how critical illness cover works
context: Critical illness cover pays a lump sum if you are diagnosed with a specified serious illness, but which illnesses are covered and how they are defined varies by insurer. Two policies can look similar and still treat the same diagnosis differently, so it is worth reading the definitions and exclusions carefully rather than comparing headline names alone.

Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA), and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute. Brokers must understand your demands and needs, explain key policy features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are looking for critical illness insurance and would like an introduction to a local insurance broker.
Explain who the cover is for, such as yourself, a partner, or your family.
Mention any health conditions or family history that might affect what you are offered, because full disclosure matters.
Describe what you want the lump sum to protect, such as your income, your mortgage, or everyday costs.
Say whether children's cover matters to you, since it is often included.
Note any preferences you have about speaking to someone locally or by phone, and what times suit you.
questions: Which serious illnesses are covered under this policy, and how are they defined?
What are the main exclusions I should understand before I decide?
How are you paid for arranging this cover, and will that be explained to me in writing?

faqs.q: What does critical illness cover actually pay for?
faqs.a: It pays a lump sum if you are diagnosed with a specified serious illness, and you can generally use the money however you need. Which illnesses are specified, and how they are defined, varies by insurer, so the policy wording is the place to check.

faqs.q: Why do definitions vary between insurers?
faqs.a: Insurers set their own wording for what counts as a specified serious illness and the severity required. That means a diagnosis covered by one policy may not meet another policy's definition, so it is worth comparing the detail rather than just the policy name.

faqs.q: Should I mention health conditions when I enquire?
faqs.a: Yes, disclose your health fully. Brokers must understand your demands and needs, and incomplete information can affect a policy later, so it is better to be open from the start.

faqs.q: How do I check that a broker is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers also belong to BIBA, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

extra_heading: How critical illness cover differs from other protection you may be offered
extra: People searching for critical illness insurance near me often end up being shown several types of protection at once, so it helps to know where critical illness sits. Critical illness cover pays a lump sum if you are diagnosed with a specified serious illness, while income protection generally replaces part of your earnings if you cannot work because of illness or injury. Life insurance pays out on death or, in some policies, on diagnosis of a terminal illness, so the three do different jobs and are not interchangeable.

A common misunderstanding is that critical illness cover works like private medical insurance. It does not pay for treatment or consultations; it pays a lump sum when a diagnosis meets the policy's definition, and you decide how to use the money. That is why the definitions and exclusions matter so much, and why an insurance broker will talk through your demands and needs rather than simply naming a policy.

Because you searched for cover near you, it is worth asking at the first appointment whether the broker deals with critical illness regularly and how they would narrow the market for your circumstances. Ask them to explain what happens if a diagnosis falls short of a policy's definition, and how children's cover and any exclusions would apply to you. If a complaint is not resolved, you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

extra_faqs.q: Is critical illness cover the same as income protection?
extra_faqs.a: No. Critical illness cover pays a lump sum on diagnosis of a specified serious illness, whereas income protection generally replaces part of your income if you cannot work. They can be arranged alongside each other, and a broker can explain how they would fit your situation.

extra_faqs.q: Will critical illness cover pay for my treatment?
extra_faqs.a: It does not pay for treatment directly. It pays a lump sum if you are diagnosed with a specified serious illness, and you choose how to use the money, whether that is covering costs while you are away from work or adapting your home.

extra_faqs.q: What should I have ready for a first conversation with a local broker?
extra_faqs.a: Be ready to explain who the cover is for, your health and family history, and what you want the lump sum to protect. Disclose your health fully, because incomplete information can affect a policy later, and ask how the broker is paid.
